binders: In the first conjunct only, rate ranges over NNReal, the nonnegative real numbers.
hypotheses: For the first conjunct, 0 < rate in the usual order inherited from Real. There are no outer hypotheses for the other three conjuncts.

Inside the definition of an admissible threshold t for any measure/function pair: X is measurable; t ≠ 0; t ≠ ∞; ω ↦ exp((X(ω))^2/(t.toReal)^2) is integrable with respect to μ; and its integral is at most 2.
conclusions: For every positive rate in NNReal, the infimum of the admissible ENNReal thresholds for n ↦ (n : Real) under poissonMeasure rate on Nat equals ∞.
The infimum of the admissible ENNReal thresholds for the identity function under expMeasure 1 on Real equals ∞.
The infimum of the admissible ENNReal thresholds for the identity function under Measure.map Real.exp (expMeasure 1) equals ∞.
The infimum of the admissible ENNReal thresholds for the identity function under cauchyMeasure 0 1 equals ∞.
mathematical_definitions: For any measurable-space-valued sample type Ω, measure μ on Ω, and function X : Ω → Real, define A(μ,X) = {t ∈ ENNReal | X is measurable, t is neither 0 nor ∞, exp(X^2/(t.toReal)^2) is μ-integrable, and ∫ exp(X^2/(t.toReal)^2) dμ ≤ 2}.
LocalDef002(μ,X) is inf A(μ,X), with the infimum taken in the complete linear order ENNReal = WithTop NNReal.

poissonMeasure r is the measure associated to poissonPMF r on Nat; expMeasure r is gammaMeasure 1 r; and cauchyMeasure x₀ γ is Dirac mass at x₀ for γ = 0 and otherwise real volume with density cauchyPDF x₀ γ.
Nat has the discrete measurable space, Real has its Borel measurable space, and the first tested function is the canonical embedding Nat → Real while the other three tested functions are identities.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Let the threshold value of a real-valued measurable function X under a measure μ be the infimum, over nonnegative extended-real t other than 0 and ∞, of those t for which exp(X^2/(t.toReal)^2) is μ-integrable and has integral at most 2. The proposition asserts all of the following simultaneously: for every strictly positive nonnegative-real rate, this threshold value for the real-valued count under the corresponding Poisson measure is ∞; it is ∞ for the identity under expMeasure 1; it is ∞ for the identity under the measure obtained by mapping expMeasure 1 through the real exponential; and it is ∞ for the identity under the Cauchy measure with location 0 and scale 1.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The only universally quantified parameter is the Poisson rate, and it is restricted to NNReal with the explicit strict-positivity hypothesis 0 < rate. The other three measure parameters are fixed exactly at 1, or at location 0 and scale 1.

Admissible thresholds are ENNReal values but explicitly exclude both 0 and ∞. Thus t.toReal is used only after those exclusions; in the standard ENNReal interpretation the remaining thresholds are finite and strictly positive.

Because LocalDef002 is a set infimum in ENNReal, an empty admissible-threshold set has infimum ∞. Since every admissible t is finite, equality of the infimum with ∞ in the standard complete order indicates that no admissible finite threshold exists; the statements may therefore be witnessed through emptiness of the set rather than attainment at ∞.
Integrability is an explicit conjunct, so the real integral inequality cannot be satisfied solely by whatever default value the integral operator assigns to a nonintegrable function.

The statement imposes measurability on X inside the threshold predicate rather than as an outer premise. If a supplied X were nonmeasurable, the admissible set would be empty and the conclusion ∞ would be vacuous; for the four displayed standard functions/measurable spaces, the dossier strongly indicates measurability but the target itself does not separately assert it.

The third measure uses Measure.map without an explicit measurability hypothesis at the target level; any nonmeasurable-function convention of that operator is hidden in its opaque wrapped definition. Real.exp is the particular mapping function here.

No explicit statement in the target asserts that the named measures are probability measures, gives their density or mass formulas, or unfolds gammaMeasure, poissonPMF, or cauchyPDF beyond the one-level bodies shown.
The proposition asserts four exact equalities to ∞ and no quantitative tail bound, moment asymptotic, centering condition, normalization condition, or comparison up to constants.
ambiguities: D009 MeasureTheory.Measure.map has an opaque one-level body (MeasureTheory.Measure.wrapped✝.1), so the packet alone does not expose its precise behavior or exceptional-case convention; describing the third measure as the usual pushforward is therefore an intended but not independently verifiable interpretation.

D053 MeasureTheory.integral likewise has an opaque one-level body (MeasureTheory.wrapped✝.1), so the packet alone does not expose its complete implementation or nonintegrable-function convention, although D052 separately requires integrability for every admissible threshold.

The packet defines expMeasure through gammaMeasure, poissonMeasure through poissonPMF, and the nondegenerate Cauchy measure through cauchyPDF, but does not unfold those three subordinate objects. Their exact parameterizations and formulas cannot be reconstructed from this dossier alone.
